subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should fatal MCP entrypoints expose one stable cross-owner diagnostic format, or may core and plugin-owned adapters retain distinct contextual prefixes?
rationale: Both designs are technically plausible, but choosing a shared format creates a new architectural and potentially user-visible contract across core and plugin ownership boundaries.

options.title: Keep Owner-Specific Diagnostics
options.body: Retain shared error normalization while allowing each entrypoint to add its own contextual prefix, closing the issue unless concrete consumer breakage is shown.

options.title: Define Shared Diagnostic Contract
options.body: Specify a generic structured diagnostic API at an approved core/plugin seam and migrate both entrypoints with focused contract tests.

recommendation.title: Keep Owner-Specific Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Retain shared error normalization while allowing each entrypoint to add its own contextual prefix, closing the issue unless concrete consumer breakage is shown.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent MCP integration history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether the shared contract is intentional.
